label: Nintendo Switch OLED Model (HEG-001)
description: Nintendo Switch OLED Model: the console itself is wireless only - Wi-Fi 802.11a/b/g/n/ac on 2.4 and 5 GHz plus Bluetooth 4.1, with no network socket on the tablet - but the bundled HEG-007 dock does add a wired LAN RJ45 that only works in TV mode, and it is USB 2.0-attached so the link is Fast Ethernet (10/100) class. The console's own ports are a USB-C system connector, a 3.5 mm headset jack and a microSD slot; the dock adds HDMI out, the LAN port and two USB 2.0 ports, and everything is mains powered with no PoE.
notes: Correction to the common assumption that the OLED Switch is Wi-Fi only: Nintendo's own tech-spec page gives the console 'Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11 a/b/g/n/ac compliant) / Bluetooth 4.1' and then, separately, 'Nintendo Switch dock with LAN port ... Wired LAN port (LAN cable sold separately.)'. Nintendo support confirms the bundled dock is model HEG-007 with 'two USB 2.0 ports, one USB-C AC Adapter port, one HDMI port, and one LAN port'. So eth0 is real but conditional: it exists only while the console is docked, and it disappears in handheld mode, where wlan0 is the only path. Nintendo publishes no LAN rate; because the dock's ports are USB 2.0 the wired link is 10/100-class, so 100M rather than 1G. wlan0 is 1x1 802.11ac (433M). No PoE.
